'''Jelena Begović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Јелена Беговић}}; born 5 June 1970) is a Serbian molecular biologist who has served as [[Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation|minister of science, technological development and innovation]] in the [[Government of Serbia|Serbian government]] from 2022 to 2025.

==Early life and academic career==
Begović was born on 5 June 1970 in [[Belgrade]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jelena Begović |url=https://imovinapoliticara.krik.rs/profil.php?id=102&ime=Jelena_Begovic |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=imovinapoliticara.krik.rs}}</ref> in what was then the [[Socialist Republic of Serbia]] in the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]]. Her family relocated to [[Addis Ababa]], [[Ethiopia]], for a few years after her birth before returning to Belgrade, where she was raised. After studying for two years at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Canada]], she graduated from the [[University of Belgrade]] Faculty of Biology (Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology), earning a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1998, a [[master's degree]] in 2002, and a [[Ph.D.]] in 2008.<ref>[https://www.najzena.rs/poznati/vesti/17740/dr-jelena-begovic-je-presla-put-od-etiopije-i-kanade-do-srbije-sada-radi-sa-najopasnijim-virusima-na-svetu-i-otkriva-kako-je-razvila-vatreno-oko/vest Marija Gavrilović, "Dr JELENA BEGOVIĆ je prešla put od Etiopije i Kanade do SRBIJE: Sada radi sa NAJOPASNIJIM virusima na svetu i otkriva kako je razvila “Vatreno oko”"], najzena.rs, 9 March 2022, accessed 18 April 2022.</ref><ref>[https://imgge.bg.ac.rs/en/jelena-begovic-en Jelena Begović], Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, accessed 18 April 2022.</ref> She has published widely in her field.

Begović became the chair of the University of Belgrade's Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering in 2014. During the early period of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]], she oversaw the opening of the "Fire Eye" lab, which tested numerous samples.<ref>[https://www.najzena.rs/poznati/vesti/17740/dr-jelena-begovic-je-presla-put-od-etiopije-i-kanade-do-srbije-sada-radi-sa-najopasnijim-virusima-na-svetu-i-otkriva-kako-je-razvila-vatreno-oko/vest Marija Gavrilović, "Dr JELENA BEGOVIĆ je prešla put od Etiopije i Kanade do SRBIJE: Sada radi sa NAJOPASNIJIM virusima na svetu i otkriva kako je razvila “Vatreno oko”"], najzena.rs, 9 March 2022, accessed 18 April 2022.</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20200503105516/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-05/03/c_139026622.htm "Feature: Chinese "Fire Eye" helps Serbia detect coronavirus"], ''Xinhua Net'', 3 May 2020, accessed 18 April 2022.</ref> In late 2021, she opened the Centre for Sequencing and Bioinformatics.<ref>"Genome sequencing center opens in Serbia, in cooperation with China," ''Xinhua English Multimedia Newswire Service'', 10 December 2021.</ref>

==Politician==
In the [[2022 Serbian parliamentary election]], the governing [[Serbian Progressive Party]] (SNS) reserved the lead positions on its ''[[Together We Can Do Everything]]'' [[electoral list]] for non-party cultural figures and academics.<ref>[https://www.blic.rs/vesti/politika/ovako-vucic-kroji-vrh-izborne-liste-sns-sta-naprednjacima-donose-danica-grujicic-i/1xdqge0 "OVAKO VUČIĆ KROJI VRH IZBORNE LISTE SNS"], ''Blic'', 14 February 2022, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref> Begović was given the third position on the list; this was [[tantamount to election]], and she was indeed elected when the list won a plurality victory with 120 out of 250 mandates.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori22/ko-su-kandidati-sns-za-narodne-poslanike/ "Ko su kandidati SNS za narodne poslanike?"], ''Danas'', 17 February 2022, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref> She was featured prominently in the SNS's billboard campaign in [[Belgrade]] during the election.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori22/lica-sa-bilborda-sns-ko-su-milan-bosnic-i-jelena-begovic-i-zasto-su-istaknuti-u-kampanji/ Aleksandra Popović, "Lica sa bilborda SNS: Ko su Milan Bosnić i Jelena Begović i zašto su istaknuti u kampanji?"], ''Danas'', 6 March 2022, accessed 18 April 2022.</ref> When the [[National Assembly (Serbia)|national assembly]] convened, she was appointed as a member of the committee on the rights of the child and a deputy member of the education committee{{efn|Formally known as the Committee on Education, Science, Technological Development, and the Information Society.}} and the environmental protection committee.<ref>[http://www.parlament.gov.rs/JELENA_BEGOVIC.1181.488.html JELENA Dr BEGOVIC], {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803220636/http://www.parlament.gov.rs/JELENA_BEGOVIC.1181.488.html |date=3 August 2022 }}, National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, accessed 15 September 2022.</ref> Her term in the assembly was brief; she resigned her seat on 3 August 2022.<ref>[http://www.parlament.gov.rs/national-assembly/composition/members-of-parliament/current-legislature.487.html Current Legislature], National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, accessed 15 September 2022.</ref>

[[Ana Brnabić]]'s third ministry was established on 26 October 2022, and Begović was appointed as the minister of science, technological development, and innovation.<ref>[https://www.rts.rs/page/stories/sr/story/9/politika/4998731/izglasana-nova-vlada-srbije.html "Izglasana nova Vlada Srbije, premijerka i ministri položili zakletvu"], ''Radio Television of Serbia'', 26 October 2022, accessed 4 January 2023.</ref>

In January 2023, Begović encouraged recipients of Serbia's Fund for Young Talents Studying Abroad to return to Serbia after their studies to contribute to the development of the country.<ref>[https://www.politika.rs/sr/clanak/531445/stipendisti "Ministarka ohrabrila studente u inostranstvu da se vrate u zemlju"], ''Politika'', 5 January 2023, accessed 5 January 2023.</ref> In September of the same year, at the initiative of Begović and [[Prime Minister of Serbia|Serbian prime minister]] Ana Brnabić, the [[United Nations General Assembly]] approved a resolution on the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development. This was the first time Serbia had initiated and coordinated the adoption of a thematic resolution at the United Nations since rejoining the institution in 2000.<ref>[https://balkangreenenergynews.com/upon-serbias-proposal-un-adopts-resolution-on-international-decade-of-sciences-for-sustainable-development/ Vladimir Spasić, "Upon Serbia’s proposal, UN adopts resolution on International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development"], ''Balkan Green Energy News'', 5 September 2023, accessed 3 April 2024. Serbia rejoined the United Nations in 2000 as part of the [[Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]].</ref>

Begović joined with [[President of Serbia|Serbian president]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] and Brnabić to launch Belgrade's BIO4 campus in December 2023. The campus is intended to become a centre of [[biotechnology]] in Europe.<ref>[https://www.srbija.gov.rs/vest/en/217398/bio4-campus-project-that-changes-serbia.php "BIO4 campus project that changes Serbia"], Government of Serbia, 27 December 2023, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref>

She was re-appointed as science minister when a new administration under [[Miloš Vučević]] was introduced on 30 April 2024.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/mandatar-milos-vucevic-saopstio-je-sastav-nove-vlade-srbije/ "Mandatar Miloš Vučević saopštio je sastav nove vlade Srbije: Sviće nova zora"], ''Danas'', 30 April 2024, accessed 1 May 2024.</ref>
